rows: Washing out / Leaching of soil constituents
Silicate clays, iron, and aluminum oxides removed

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: A soil profile is a vertical section of soil extending through all its horizons from the surface to the underlying parent rock.
The O Horizon is dominated by organic matter, primarily found in undisturbed forest soils.
The Solum comprises the true soil layers (A, E, and B) where active pedogenic processes occur.
Eluviation (washing out) defines the E horizon, whereas Illuviation (accumulation) defines the B horizon.
Regolith represents the entire mantle of loose, weathered material overlying unweathered bedrock (R horizon).
Vertical Sequence: O -> A -> E -> B -> C -> R (frequently asked in sequence ordering questions).
Distinguish Eluviation (E horizon: removal of clay and oxides) from Illuviation (B horizon: deposition of washed-down materials).
Key Definition: Solum = A + E + B horizons, whereas Regolith = Solum + C horizon.
